sDescription: English indie pop band Blossoms scored their fourth UK No.1 album whith their fifth studio album Gary. The album also debuted atop the UK's Vinyl Albums Chart and Record Store Chart, and was noted for having 86% of its total debut sales coming from physical formats. The album and title track were named after a fibreglass gorilla statue of the same name, which was stolen from a garden centre in Lanarkshire, Scotland in 2023.

American singer, songwriter Marty Balin died at the age of 76. He was best known as the founder and one of the lead singers of Jefferson Airplane and Jefferson Starship who had the 1967 US No.18 single 'White Rabbit'. Balin played with Jefferson Airplane at the Monterey Pop Festival in 1967 and at the Woodstock Festival in 1969.

Lil Wayne became the new king of the Billboard Hot 100 by placing his 109th song on the chart as an artist. The rapper featured on Game's latest track 'Celebration.' Elvis Presley, with 108 entries, had held the title for 45 years.

Tony Bennett became the oldest living person to top the US album chartwhen the 85-year-old's 'Duets II' album went to No.1. The record, which featured collaborations with Amy Winehouse and Lady Gaga, was also his first US No.1 in his 60 year career. The previous oldest performer to top the chart was Bob Dylan in 2009 with 'Together Through Life'. At the time he was 67-years old.
Metallica started a three-week run at No.1 on the US album chart with 'Death Magnetic', the bands ninth studio album.

Pink Floyd's manager Bryan Morrison died after spending over two years in a coma. Morrison suffered severe brain injuries in a polo accident at the Royal Berkshire Polo Club, England in 2006, and never recovered. He also managed The Pretty Things and was a music publisher for Syd Barrett, The Bee Gees, Elton John, The Jam T-Rex and Wham!

Jamie Lyons, lead singer of Music Explosion, died of a heart attack at the age of 57. The band scored the garage-band classic 'Little Bit o' Soul', which spent 16 weeks on the Billboard Pop chart in 1967, peaking at #2.

Legendary record producer Phil Spector was formally charged with murder in the February 3rd, 2003 shooting of actress Lana Clarkson. He was convicted in April, 2009 and sentenced to 19 years to life in the California State prison system.

Kylie Minogue called in police to investigate a series of threatening letters. The singer became concerned after receiving 700 letters at her home and office. The letters started as ordinary fan mail but became increasingly aggressive.

Thieves broke into Jerry Hall's Richmond home and stole jewellery worth £7000 and a laptop computer. Two of Jerry's children were asleep at the time while the ex Mrs Jagger was on stage appearing in the West End Show, The Graduate.
The Manic Street Preachers scored their first UK No.1 album with their fifth album 'This Is My Truth Tell Me Yours'.
Dee Dee Ramone of the Ramones was arrested for possessing marijuana during a drug bust in New York's Greenwich Village.
The Beatles track Twist and Shout re-entered the US singles chart over twenty-five years after it first appeared after the song was featured in the film Ferris Bueller's Day Off.

Metallica bass player Cliff Burton was crushed to death after the bands tour bus crashed between Stockholm and Copenhagen. During a European tour members from the band drew cards for the most comfortable bunk on the tour bus, Burton had won the game with an Ace of Spades and was asleep when the tour bus ran over a patch of black ice and skidded off of the road. He was thrown through the window of the bus, which fell on top of him.

David Bowie scored his fourth UK No.1 album with his fourteenth studio album Scary Monsters (And Supercreeps). The album's lead single, 'Ashes to Ashes', revisited the character of Major Tom from 'Space Oddity' and was promoted with an inventive music video, at the time the most expensive music video ever made.

Scottish guitarist Jimmy McCullough died from a heroin overdose in his flat in Maida Vale, London, aged 26. Member of Stone The Crows, Thunderclap Newman and Wings (1974 to 1977). When 'Something in the Air' by Thunderclap Newman went to No.1 in 1969, it made McCulloch the youngest guitarist to ever play on a UK No.1 single, as he was was just sixteen years old at the time.
Eric Clapton sponsored a West Bromwich Albion UEFA cup-tie against Galatasarey of Turkey. After the game, Eric presented each player with a gold copy of his latest album 'Slowhand''

Rory Storm singer from UK 60s group Rory Storm and the Hurricanes died aged 32 after taking an overdose of sleeping pills in a suicide pact with his mother. Ringo Starr played drums with Storm before joining The Beatles.

Pink Floyd appeared at the Queen's Hall in Dunoon, Scotland. Due to bad weather, all the ferries to Dunoon were cancelled, so Pink Floyd hired their own boat from Gourock and risked the rough seas to make the crossing, eventually appearing in front of 400 fans.

Working on new songs The Beatles recorded various parts for the new John Lennon song ‘I Am The Walrus’ and the new Paul McCartney song ‘Fool On The Hill.’ Lennon received a letter from a pupil at Quarry Bank High School, that mentioned an English teacher was making his class analyse Beatles' lyrics. Lennon, amused that a teacher was putting so much effort into understanding the Beatles' lyrics, decided to write in his next song the most confusing lyrics that he could.
The Beach Boys made their TV debut on 'The Ed Sullivan Show' on US TV where they performed their first US No.1 single 'I Get Around' and 'Wendy'.

Canadian singer and songwriter Avril Lavigne. She had the 2002 US & UK No.3 single 'Complicated' and 2002 US No.2 & UK No.1 debut album is the best-selling album of the 21st century by a Canadian artist. Her 2007 worldwide No.1 single 'Girlfriend' was a worldwide success, peaking at the top spot of the charts in eight countries, including Australia, New Zealand, Canada and was Lavigne's first No.1 song in the United States. Lavigne is the youngest female to top the charts, aged 17 years and 3 months.

American rapper Lil Wayne, (Dwayne Michael Carter, Jr.). His sixth album, Tha Carter III (2008), yielded the pinnacle of Wayne's career, with first-week sales of over one million units domestically. It won the Best Rap Album at the 51st Annual Grammy Awards and was supported by his first US No.1 single 'Lollipop' (featuring Static Major). He is often regarded as one of the most influential hip hop artists of his generation, as well as one of the greatest rappers of all time.

American musician Bradley Arnold the lead singer and a founding member of the Mississippi-based rock band 3 Doors Down. The band was brought to mainstream popularity with their 2000 debut single, 'Kryptonite', which peaked at No.3 on the Billboard Hot 100.

English singer, songwriter Lee Brennan. With the boyband 911 he had the 1998 UK No.2 single 'More Than A Woman'. 911 sold 10 million singles and 6 million albums around the world and were very popular in Southeast Asia, where their first two albums went to No.1.

American musician and actress Carrie Brownstein. She first came to prominence as a member of the band Excuse 17 before forming the rock trio Sleater-Kinney. Sleater-Kinney originated as part of the riot grrrl movement and has become a key part of the American indie rock scene.
Mark Calderon, from American R&B group Color Me Badd who had the 1991 UK No.1 single 'I Wanna Sex You Up', and the 1991 US No.1 single 'I Adore Mi Amor'.
American singer, guitarist Stephan Jenkins, the frontman of the alternative rock band Third Eye Blind who had the 1997 US No.4 & UK No.33 single 'Semi-Charmed Life'.

American singer, actor, writer, and producer Shaun Cassidy. He had the 1977 US No.1 single 'Da Doo Ron Ron'. Shaun is the half-brother of David Cassidy. He has created and produced a number of television series including American Gothic, Roar and Invasion.

American bass guitarist and record producer Robbie Shakespeare. He is best known as one half of the reggae rhythm section and production duo Sly and Robbie, with drummer Sly Dunbar. Regarded as one of the most influential reggae bassists, Shakespeare's work extended beyond the reggae genre, covering various pop and rock artists such as Mick Jagger, Bob Dylan, Jackson Browne, Cyndi Lauper, Joe Cocker, Yoko Ono, Serge Gainsbourg, and Grace Jones. He died on 8 December 2021 age 68.

Australian musician Greg Ham who with Men At Work had the 1983 UK and US No.1 single 'Down Under'. He played saxophone, flute, organ, piano, and synthesizer. Ham was found dead on 19 April 2012 age 58 at his home in Carlton North, Melbourne, Australia.

English singer, songwriter and musician Linda Lewis. As well as a solo career, Lewis also provided backing vocals for other artists, including David Bowie, Al Kooper, Cat Stevens, Rick Wakeman, Rod Stewart, Joan Armatrading and Jamiroquai. She died on 3 May 2023 age 72.

Russ Kunkel, American drummer and producer who has worked as a session musician with many popular artists, including Jackson Browne, Joni Mitchell, Jimmy Buffett, Neil Dimond, Bob Dylan, Carole King, Stevie Nicks, Linda Ronstadt, Bob Seger, Carly Simon and Stephen Stills.

American musician, singer, songwriter, record producer, and actor Meat Loaf (Marvin Lee Aday). His record breaking 1978 album Bat Out Of Hell spent 457 weeks on the UK album chart. His Bat Out of Hell trilogy of albums (consisting of Bat Out of Hell, Bat Out of Hell II: Back into Hell, and Bat Out of Hell III: The Monster Is Loose) has sold more than 50 million copies worldwide. Meat Loaf has also appeared in over 50 movies and television shows. He died on 20 January 2022 aged 74.

Scottish singer and actress Barbara Dickson, who had the 1985 UK No.1 single with Elaine Paige, 'I Know Him So Well'. Dickson has placed fifteen albums on the UK Albums Chart from 1977 to date, and has had a number of hit singles, including four which reached the top 20 on the UK Singles Chart.

English rock singer and stage actor Bernard Jewry known professionally as Shane Fenton and later as Alvin Stardust. He had the 1974 UK No.1 single 'Jealous Mind', plus 10 other UK Top 40 singles. He died on 23 October 2014 age 72.

Randy Bachman, lead guitarist, songwriter from Canadian rock band Guess Who who had the 1970 US No.1 & UK No.19 single 'American Woman'. He later formed Bachman Turner Overdrive who had the 1974 US No.1 & UK No.2 single 'You Ain't Seen Nothing Yet'.

American jazz pianist, keyboardist and arranger Bob Harris. He played with The Turtles and The Friends of Distinction and was a member of Frank Zappa's band The Mothers for a short time in 1971. At the end of the 1970s, Harris toured with Ray Charles. He died from the effects of a drug overdose on August 11, 2001.
